title: Künneth–Verdier isomorphism
statement:
The three maps of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] are isomorphisms, natural in their
variables, under the hypotheses of that definition (the $Rf_i^!$ are the
constructible exceptional adjoints of [sk-def-sf-operations] (vi); no
admissibility datum of [sk-def-sf-admissible] is assumed): the
exceptional Künneth map $\alpha$, the external Hom map $\beta$, and the
Künneth–Verdier map $\kappa$. In particular, for $X,Y$ separated of finite
type over $k$, with the structure
morphism $a_Y$ and the product projection $p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y$
as in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), and
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$,

$$
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr).
$$

proof.text: Work first with A=A_{E,n}. First work on separated finite-type schemes over the fixed algebraically closed field, with inputs in $D^b_{ctf}$. Step 5 below extends $\alpha$ to the possibly nonseparated finite-type schemes allowed by the map definition, and Step 7 does the same for $\beta$. The preservation assertions of [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)-(v) justify pullback, tensor, internal Hom, both direct images and exceptional inverse image on this category. In particular ordinary direct images used below remain bounded and finite Tor. Use the actual constructible adjoints [sk-def-sf-operations](vi), not an unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint. Write P_f=Rf_! and G_f=Rf^!. Compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the adjunctions identify G_{gf} with G_f G_g: both represent Hom(P_g P_f(-),K). By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] the comparison is an isomorphism, and its counit is epsilon_g composed with P_g(epsilon_f). This last formula follows by transposing the identity through the two adjunctions, or [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2). The same calculation gives identity comparisons and fixes their normalization. Thus no existence or admissibility hypothesis has been added. For later use of [prop-sf-dualizable-hom], the finite operations here do give the datum [def-sf-datum] on separated finite-type schemes, rather than assuming its axioms: (A1) is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) for ordinary adjoints and [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) for constructible exceptional adjoints, with the pasted counits just calculated; (A2) for compact support is [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], applicable since [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies an etale-origin witness for every input. For proper maps the compactification with identity open gives $Rf_!=Rf_*$, so this also proves the proper ordinary case; the smooth ordinary case is [fix-lem-exchanges](3). (A3) is [fix-prop-projection-formula]; (A4) is the composition theorem and the same identity-open compactification. (A5) on these finite-Tor domains is [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii), with the map/coherence assertions of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2),(4). (A6) is [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vi). Thus the datum hypotheses of that evaluation lemma have been verified by separate statements. No datum of ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility is involved.

source.place: alpha: the constructible adjunctions and composition comparisons

proof.text: We record the composition check for alpha, rather than treating a general square mate as invertible. Ku_! is the product comparison specified in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i); its factors are compact-support base change and projection formula. Substitute these factors for two composable pairs (f_1,f_2) and (g_1,g_2). The horizontal and vertical exchange identities [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4) combine the two base changes into that for (g_1 f_1,g_2 f_2), and the composition assertion of [fix-prop-projection-formula] combines their two projection maps. Tensor associativity and symmetry merely rebracket the four factors. Consequently the two product comparisons for P_{g_1}P_{f_1} and P_{g_2}P_{f_2} equal the product comparison for the composites under P_g P_f=P_{gf}. Now transpose the composite of the two alpha maps: substitute their defining transposes Ku_! followed by epsilon_1 boxtimes epsilon_2. Its transpose is Ku_! for the composite followed in each factor by epsilon_{g_i} P_{g_i}(epsilon_{f_i}), the composite counit of Step 1. This is exactly the defining transpose of alpha for the composite. The Hom bijection proves equality, not just isomorphism of the two endpoints. For an identity pair, the identity exchange and projection comparisons reduce $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ to the tensor-unit comparison; the identity counits reduce its transpose to the identity of $L_1\boxtimes L_2$, so alpha is the identity. For interchange of the factors, apply tensor symmetry to the defining transpose: naturality of symmetry sends $\varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2$ to $\varepsilon_2\boxtimes\varepsilon_1$, and substitution of the exchange/projection factors in $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ interchanges those two factors with their signed tensor symmetry. The resulting transpose is precisely the definition of alpha for $(f_2,f_1)$ under the product-swap isomorphisms. Injectivity of transposition gives the asserted interchange equality. We may therefore compose identity-factor comparisons to obtain alpha for a general pair.

source.place: alpha: the composition/counit coherence implicit in the affine factorization argument

proof.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, let $F=f\times\mathrm{id}_Z$, and write $r:X\times Z\to X$, $s:Y\times Z\to Y$. Put $\omega_f=G_fA_Y$. By [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](1),(3), its canonical tensor map $\theta_{f,K}:f^*K\otimes^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fK$ is invertible and the canonical base-change map $b:r^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_F$ is invertible. Their precise counit transposes are given in [def-pur-co-smoothness](2),(3): $\theta$ transposes to inverse projection formula followed by the coefficient counit, and $b$ transposes to $s^*\varepsilon_{f,A}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$. For arbitrary $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, form
$$
G_fK\boxtimes Q\xrightarrow{\theta_{f,K}^{-1}\boxtimes1}
F^*(K\boxtimes Q)\otimes^L r^*\omega_f
\xrightarrow{1\otimes b}F^*(K\boxtimes Q)\otimes^L\omega_F
\xrightarrow{\theta_{F,K\boxtimes Q}}G_F(K\boxtimes Q).
$$
The reassociation here uses [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Every arrow is an isomorphism. This composite is the specified $\alpha_{f,\mathrm{id}}$: transpose it under $P_F\dashv G_F$ and substitute the two displayed transposes from the definition of cohomological smoothness. Naturality of the projection map moves the $K,Q$ factors past the coefficient counit. Its base-change square commutes: using the compactification definition [def-exchange-projection], the proper-factor square is [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality]; for the open factor both orders are the same tensor map on the open and zero off the open, by the extension-by-zero definition. Thus the result of the substitution is exactly $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by $\varepsilon_{f,K}\boxtimes1_Q$, the transpose in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii). This proves equality of the specified maps by injectivity of transposition. The purity orientation used in the unit route is the diagonal/DNC one: [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] identifies $G_fK$ with $f^*K(d)[2d]$ through [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], whose tensor map is precisely this $\theta$. The argument therefore proves the smooth step of that route for arbitrary coefficients without mistaking a purity-defined exchange for an adjunction mate. Pure relative dimensions may be treated separately on the open-and-closed components of a smooth map.

source.place: alpha: smooth purity and its base-change compatibility, strengthened to arbitrary auxiliary coefficients

proof.text:
Next let i:C\toY be closed with complement j:U\toY, put I=i times id_Z and J=j times id_Z, and take arbitrary K,Q as above. Apply [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] to K and to K boxtimes Q. Tensor the first distinguished triangle externally with Q. By [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star] for i and j its terms identify with
 R I_*(i^!K boxtimes Q) \to K boxtimes Q \to R J_*(j^*K boxtimes Q) \to [1].
The second localization triangle is
 R I_* I^!(K boxtimes Q) \to K boxtimes Q \to R J_* J^*(K boxtimes Q) \to [1].
The last terms agree since J^*(K boxtimes Q)=j^*K boxtimes Q; the middle comparison is the identity. The first comparison is R I_*(alpha_{i,id}). To verify this rather than choose a triangle completion, transpose under I_* dashv I^!: its counit square is exactly the external tensor of i_*i^!K\toK. For a closed immersion P_i=Ri_* and the proper projection/base-change maps in Ku_! are the ordinary ones, so this transpose is the definition in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii). The second square is the equality of the adjunction units defining the canonical ordinary product comparison (transpose both maps under J^* dashv RJ_*; both are the pullback of K boxtimes Q). Here is the missing connecting-square check. Rotate both triangles and use (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] on the identity middle comparison and the identified last comparison to obtain a triangle morphism with some first arrow $a_0$. Let $a=RI_*(\alpha_{i,\mathrm{id}})$. The counit square just checked says $(a-a_0)$ becomes zero after composition into the middle vertex. Exactness of Hom into the second triangle, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], factors $a-a_0$ through its last vertex shifted by $[-1]$. This factorization is zero: by the ordinary adjunction [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), $\operatorname{Hom}(RI_*T,RJ_*B[-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(J^*RI_*T,B[-1])=0$. Indeed $J^*RI_*T=0$: restriction to the complementary open removes the entire closed support, as one sees directly from closed direct image on sheaves. Thus $a=a_0$, and the specified first arrow does form a morphism of distinguished triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] the first comparison is an isomorphism. Finally the unit T\toI^! I_*T is an isomorphism by [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages], so I_* reflects isomorphisms: apply I^! and these units. Thus alpha_{i,id}(K,Q) is an isomorphism, with no regularity hypothesis on i. In the regular smooth pairs explicitly mentioned in the unit, [sk-thm-regular](c) supplies the class-normalized isomorphism $Ri^!A=A_C(-c)[-2c]$, and (d) identifies the product class with the exterior product of the two classes. The just-verified counit square is the defining transpose for the class-normalized product map as well. Hence in this case the localization comparison is the fundamental-class product comparison required by the unit. This normalization uses regularity only in this regular special case; the preceding localization proof covers arbitrary closed immersions. For clarity, the tensor transport just used is monoidal: apply the general ringed-topos tensor-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the comparison morphism $\nu$ with the constant coefficient ring. Its inverse image is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], so the constructible equivalence from etale origin is an exact monoidal equivalence on the objects under consideration.

source.place: alpha: supported localization and the closed-immersion unit; explicit triangle argument

proof.text: The comparisons are local on source and target in the Zariski topology. Indeed for an open immersion u, purity in relative dimension zero identifies G_u=u^*. For a Cartesian square with open horizontal maps u:X'\toX and v:Y'\toY, the composition comparisons of Step 1 applied to fu=vf' give u^*G_f=G_{f'}v^*. Applied to the defining transpose of alpha, the same composition calculation in Step 2 gives its restriction. This is a consequence of composition with open exceptional pullbacks; it does not assert that an arbitrary square mate is invertible. Isomorphy can be tested on these opens: the cohomology sheaves of the cone restrict to zero, hence are zero on an open cover. Choose affine opens V in Y and W in f^{-1}V covering X. For W=Spec B and V=Spec R, finite type supplies finitely many algebra generators b_1,...,b_r of B over R. The surjection R[t_1,...,t_r]\toB defines a closed immersion W\toA^r_V whose composite with the smooth projection to V is f|_W. Steps 3 and 4, and the composition identity of Step 2, prove alpha_{f,id} on this chart for arbitrary restrictions of K,Q. Local detection proves it globally. Applying this result to (f_1,id_{Y_2}) and (id_{X_1},f_2), and composing, proves alpha_{f_1,f_2} for arbitrary L_1,L_2. This uses exactly the blueprint's closed-immersion/smooth-projection factorization, with the stronger arbitrary-coefficient localization calculation, so no support-dimension induction is necessary. There is no extra separatedness hypothesis on $X_i,Y_i$ hidden here. For a possibly nonseparated finite-type scheme, take affine opens in each $Y_i$, affine opens in their inverse images in $X_i$, and affine opens in the auxiliary scheme $Z$. On the ordinary etale site, [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] says that a separated etale $u$ has exact $u_!\dashv u^*$ on the whole derived category and $u^*f^\times=(fu)^\times$. Applied also to $v$, uniqueness of the right adjoint to the equality $fu=vf'$ gives $u^*f^\times=f'^\times v^*$. The finite functor in [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) is the transport of this ordinary etale functor; [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] identify the constructible finite-Tor objects on the two sites. Thus the open restrictions just used are available even before any separated-scheme preservation theorem is applied. Compact-support pasting [fix-lem-exchanges](2) and the counit definition of $\alpha$ identify the restricted map with the map on these affine charts. All geometric operations needed for its invertibility now occur on separated schemes, the case already proved. The resulting opens cover the product, and one may choose a finite subcover: every finite-type scheme here is Noetherian and quasi-compact, as justified below. Preservation on these separated charts also supplies preservation on the original corners, rather than merely isomorphism detection. On each chart the restricted exceptional values have bounded constructible cohomology and a finite Tor interval by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](v). Take the minimum lower bound and maximum upper bound over the finite cover. Cohomology and tensor with an arbitrary module sheaf restrict to the same chart constructions, so these bounds hold globally. Constructibility is local for this finite cover: the finitely many constructible strata on its opens form a finite constructible partition after common refinement, with the same local models. Thus the exceptional values are in $D^b_{ctf}$ on the nonseparated corners as well. A cone zero on the product opens has every cohomology sheaf zero, by the sheaf axiom, and is zero. This proves $\alpha$ on the full domain in the item. Source error (STATEMENT-DISPUTED, proof inference only): the imported sentence taking a closed immersion $g_i:Z_i=\operatorname{supp}L_i\hookrightarrow Y_i$ is invalid when support means nonzero stalks. For $j:\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$ and $L=j_!A$, that support is $\mathbf G_m$, not a closed subscheme. If support instead means its closure, the equality needs to be stated and justified with that closure. We use the same smooth/closed/affine route with the arbitrary-coefficient localization calculation above; it proves the conclusion directly before this invalid support induction, so the theorem statement is unchanged. The locality lemma's Noetherian/compactifiability hypotheses are justified as follows: a field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole field; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] then makes every finite-type scheme here Noetherian. Such a scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (intersections of its affine opens are opens in a Noetherian space, hence quasi-compact). [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications for the separated finite-type maps $f$, $fu$, and $f'$. Thus the ordinary-etale locality theorem is applied on its stated domain.

source.place: alpha: affine factorization and etale/open localization; elementary affine-algebra construction spelled out

proof.text: For beta remain at the finite ring A. Both its source and target are contravariant exact in each $E_i$: internal Hom is exact with its signed shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] (Stacks Tags 08J9, 08JB, 08JC); external tensor is exact by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], transported from etale to pro-etale finite-Tor objects using [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. The evaluation-defined transformation respects these signs because it is the tensor-Hom transpose in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iii). Its isomorphism locus in either E_i is therefore triangulated by [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three], and closed under retracts since a retract of an isomorphism is an isomorphism (retract its inverse). The finite-ring generation assertion of [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] now reduces successively in E_1 and E_2 to E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i, where h_i is a locally closed immersion and F_i is lisse with finite projective stalks. These generators are in D^b_ctf by that assertion. Put F_i^vee=Hom_A(F_i,A), in degree zero. The finite datum was verified in Step 1, so [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] applies to these degree-zero site-perfect $F_i$ and gives the canonical evaluation isomorphism. Concretely, locally $F_i$ is a direct summand of $A^{r_i}$; for a free module evaluation identifies Hom(A^{r_i},T) with T^{r_i}, including the complexes and their differentials. The same identity on the two complementary idempotent summands gives RHom(F_i,T)=F_i^vee tensor^L T for every T, and F_i^vee is flat constructible. This also proves (F_1 boxtimes F_2)^vee=F_1^vee boxtimes F_2^vee. These local identities are identities for the evaluation maps and glue. No assertion that every constructible finite-Tor object is site-perfect, or that every adic lisse sheaf has a finite trivializing cover, is used. For clarity, the tensor transport just used is monoidal: apply the general ringed-topos tensor-pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the comparison morphism $\nu$ with the constant coefficient ring. Its inverse image is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], so the constructible equivalence from etale origin is an exact monoidal equivalence on the objects under consideration.

source.place: beta: devissage in the first variables and the finite-projective evaluation calculation

proof.text:
Write h=h_1 times h_2, F=F_1 boxtimes F_2 and L=L_1 boxtimes L_2. The natural tensor-Hom comparison [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] and Step 6 identify RHom(E_i,L_i) with Rh_{i*}(F_i^vee tensor^L h_i^!L_i). Put $T_i=F_i^\vee\otimes^Lh_i^!L_i$, so $T_i\in D^b_{ctf}(S_i,A)$, where $h_i:S_i\to Y_i$, and $Rh_{i*}T_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,A)$ by Step 1. The first application of [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star], with $f=h_1$ and auxiliary coefficient $Rh_{2*}T_2$ on $Y_2$, gives
$$
Rh_{1*}T_1\boxtimes Rh_{2*}T_2\xrightarrow{\sim}
R(h_1\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_2})_*(T_1\boxtimes Rh_{2*}T_2).
$$
The second application, with $f=h_2$ and auxiliary coefficient $T_1$ on $S_1$, followed by product symmetry, gives
$$
T_1\boxtimes Rh_{2*}T_2\xrightarrow{\sim}
R(\mathrm{id}_{S_1}\times h_2)_*(T_1\boxtimes T_2).
$$
Apply $R(h_1\times\mathrm{id}_{Y_2})_*$ to this arrow and use the ordinary composition comparison of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3). The composite morphism is $h_1\times h_2$, and $T_1\boxtimes T_2=F^\vee\otimes^L(h_1^!L_1\boxtimes h_2^!L_2)$ by the monoidal pullback comparison and tensor symmetry. These are the two ordinary Kunneth arrows in the following chain. This gives
 RHom(E_1,L_1) boxtimes RHom(E_2,L_2)
 \to Rh_*((F_1^vee boxtimes F_2^vee) tensor^L (h_1^!L_1 boxtimes h_2^!L_2))
 \to Rh_*(F^vee tensor^L h^!L)
 = Rh_*RHom(F,h^!L)
 = RHom(Rh_!F,L)
 = RHom(E_1 boxtimes E_2,L).
The second arrow is Rh_*(1 tensor alpha), invertible by Step 5; the final equality uses Ku_! of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i). Every arrow is an isomorphism. These inputs satisfy the domains of the cited nodes by Step 1. Check that this chain is the canonical beta, as follows. Put $B=\RHom(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes\RHom(E_2,L_2)$. The bijections actually used are
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rh_*\RHom(F,h^!L))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h^*B\otimes^LF,h^!L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rh_!(h^*B\otimes^LF),L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes^LRh_!F,L).
$$
They are ordinary adjunction plus tensor-Hom, exceptional adjunction, and the projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula], respectively. With $Rh_!F=E_1\boxtimes E_2$, compare the image of the displayed composite under this bijection with the evaluation transpose defining $\beta$. This is a comparison under bijections, not detection of equality by pullback. The tensor-Hom comparison sends evaluation on Rh_!F_i to the composite Rh_{i!}(F_i tensor RHom(F_i,h_i^!L_i))\toRh_{i!}h_i^!L_i\toL_i. The ordinary product comparisons transpose to the ordinary counits. Finally alpha transposes, by definition, to Ku_! followed by epsilon_{h_1} boxtimes epsilon_{h_2}. Thus the composite transpose is the external tensor of the two preceding evaluation composites, with precisely the symmetry interchanging F_2 and its neighboring Hom factor. This is the defining transpose of beta. The triangle identities cancel the inserted units and counits; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2) permits the successive transposes with these composite adjunctions. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijections proves equality of the morphisms. Hence beta is invertible on the generators, and Step 6 proves it for all E_i. For possibly nonseparated $Y_i$, restrict $\beta$ to products of affine opens. The slice-restriction assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and the monoidal restriction of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify the restrictions of both endpoints and of their evaluation transpose with $\beta$ on those separated charts. Its cone therefore has zero cohomology on a covering, hence zero cohomology everywhere. This proves $\beta$ on the full finite-coefficient domain without applying separated-scheme preservation to a nonseparated scheme.

source.place: beta: the displayed two ordinary Kunneth maps followed by alpha; explicit evaluation/counit check

proof.text: Pass from finite coefficients to integral and field coefficients only after the preceding proof. At O_E, [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii) supplies constructible finite-Tor values and canonical finite reductions for general internal Hom and exceptional inverse image, preserving evaluation and adjunction maps. Pullback, tensor and the compact-support maps commute with integral reduction by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; [fix-lem-exchanges] and [fix-prop-projection-formula] give the corresponding reductions of the constituent Ku_! maps. Thus the reductions of the specified alpha and beta, not merely of their endpoints, are the finite-level alpha and beta. The cone of either integral comparison belongs to the derived-complete constructible category by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] and has zero finite reductions. Its Roos triangle in [def-weil-derived-complete] is therefore C\to0\to0\toC[1], which forces C=0. Both integral comparisons are isomorphisms. At E the operations and maps are their scalar localizations by [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; localize their inverses to obtain inverses. At Qbar choose one finite extension containing the finitely many coefficient fields of the inputs and represent all maps there; the common-stage formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the operation/evaluation transports of [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii) and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify the comparison with the one already proved over this field. Its inverse represents an inverse over Qbar as well. The assertions also survive retracts if an idempotent-completed coefficient presentation is used, by restricting the inverse to the same idempotents. No reduction of a rational object modulo varpi is asserted. For a possibly nonseparated corner, first restrict to the affine charts of Steps 5 and 7. Reduction and the completed pullback/tensor constructions are restrictions of the same coefficient towers, and internal Hom restricts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Exceptional restriction is the finite open-adjunction comparison of Step 5 level by level in the construction of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi). Hence on each such chart the reductions of the specified comparisons are those just proved invertible. Apply the complete-cone argument on those charts, then use vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of the global cone on the resulting covering. The field and common-stage construction has the same restriction property. Thus the use of the separated-chart stability theorem has not strengthened the theorem's hypotheses.

source.place: all three maps: coefficient passage; finite proof followed by derived-complete conservativity and scalar localization

proof.text: At each coefficient stage apply beta to (E_1,L_1)=(Lambda_X,M) and (E_2,L_2)=(N,omega_Y). The tensor-unit identities identify its source with M boxtimes D_Y N and its first target with RHom(p_Y^*N,M boxtimes omega_Y). The isomorphism alpha_{id_X,a_Y} identifies M boxtimes omega_Y with Rp_X^!M. Applying RHom(1,-) and composing gives exactly kappa of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iv). Both factors are isomorphisms, so kappa is an isomorphism. Naturality in every variable follows from the evaluation transposes defining beta and from the counit transposes defining alpha: both Hom bijections are natural, so transposing a natural composite gives a natural map. Composition and coefficient transport preserve these specified maps, as checked above. Empty schemes or a zero input give zero objects on both sides, so these edge cases require no dimension or support convention.
